introduction.text: The Mitreo della Planta Pedis is a Mithraeum located in Ostia, Rome, notable for its early 3rd‑century construction and its archaeological evidence of the Mithraic cult.

history.description: The Mitreo della Planta Pedis was constructed at the beginning of the 3rd century AD in Ostia.
A coin of Emperor Valerian (reigned 253–259 AD) bearing the emperor and Sol was found in the Mitreo.

design.description: The sanctuary is a three‑nave hall built in opus latericium and opus vittatum, with pillars separating the nave and a cult niche at the back.

art.description: Mosaics in the entrance hall include a serpent and a footprint of Mithra, geometric patterns, and a footprint of Mithra's foot.
Reliefs in the cult niche depict the personifications of Sol and Luna.
